A 24-lecture course (plus a 3-part probability primer) that maps the modern deep-learning stack — from the probability under every loss, through CNNs and Transformers, to LLMs, diffusion, and 2026 frontier topics.

Every lecture follows the same rhythm · a pop-quiz hook · worked numerics · linked interactives · canonical references · 6 practice problems. New to the material? Start with the **[L00 primer](html/lec00-probability-mle-recap-lecture.html)**, then open any deck from the **[Slides](slides.qmd)** page.

## Course at a glance

The course splits into a **spine** (L00–L14 · mastery) and a **landscape** (L15–L24 · literacy).

- **Module 0 · Probabilistic foundations** · *L00–L00C* — distributions → MLE → MAP → information theory: where every loss and regularizer comes from.
- **Module 1 · Foundations & deep networks** · *L1–L3* — why depth, universal approximation, training in practice.
- **Module 2 · Optimization** · *L4–L5* — SGD, momentum, Adam, learning-rate schedules.
- **Module 3 · Regularization** · *L6* — double descent, dropout, normalization (spans two sessions).
- **Module 4 · CNNs & visual recognition** · *L7–L9* — modern CNNs, transfer learning, detection & segmentation.
- **Module 5 · Sequence models** · *L10–L11* — RNNs / LSTMs, seq2seq, and the attention bottleneck.
- **Module 6 · Attention & Transformers** · *L12–L14* — attention, the Transformer built live, tokenization.
- **Module 7 · LLMs** · *L15–L16* — scaling laws, alignment, LoRA / RLHF / DPO.
- **Module 8 · Self-supervised & vision-language** · *L17–L18* — contrastive learning, CLIP.
- **Module 9 · Generative models** · *L19–L22* — VAEs, GANs, diffusion (theory + practice).
- **Module 10 · Wrap-up** · *L23–L24* — efficient inference, and the frontier: agents, reasoning, interpretability.

The full schedule with slide links is on the **[Slides](slides.qmd)** page; the chapter-by-chapter reading map is on the **[Syllabus](syllabus.qmd)**.

## What you'll build

Two code threads run end-to-end through the course:

- **Language** · micrograd → MLP → Transformer → nanoGPT → LoRA fine-tune
- **Vision** · MLP-MNIST → CNN-CIFAR → transfer-ResNet → ViT-CLIP → diffusion

Running examples · cat / not-cat · MNIST · CIFAR-10 · Tiny Shakespeare · CelebA.

The course follows **Prince · [*Understanding Deep Learning*](https://udlbook.github.io/udlbook/)** (2023, free PDF) — see [Resources](resources.qmd) for the full book / video / blog map.
